name: Messianism
summary: Messianism is the belief in the coming of a messiah, an agent of divine salvation who will deliver a people from oppression and inaugurate an age of justice and peace. In its classical Jewish form the messiah is an anointed king of David's line who restores Israel's kingdom; Christian, Islamic and other traditions have their own messiah figures, and modern thinkers turned the hope into a secular idea of progress. Its sources describe a hope about history rather than a programme for running a society, so they settle very few of the test's statements.
scope: The belief in a messiah and a messianic age as the three defining reference works describe it: the Israelite and Jewish messianic hope (Davidic king, restoration, the messianic age) as the core, with Britannica's note that other religions have restorer figures and that modern liberal thinkers secularised the idea. Particular messianic movements and religions, and the political programmes of any group that holds a messianic belief, are other subjects and are excluded.
